newsitem.title: FINLAND: Kone highlights growth in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Kone highlights growth in Asia.

text.p: Finnish elevator maker Kone Oy said on Friday it will continue to grow in Asia and a plant it has said it will build in China would help.
"We intend to continue to grow in Asia, and an important component of that is a factory in China," CEO Anssi Soila told a news conference after Kone's 1996 results.
Kone reported 1996 profit after financial items down to 124 million markka from 202 million in 1995 and said its earnings for this year would only "improve somewhat."
Its sales in Asia rose 50 percent in 1996, but Soila said the growth would show up in the books with about a year's delay as deliveries were made.
"The growth has been terrific. We have grown faster than the market," he said.
Looking at other business, Soila said elevator modernisation accounted for 15 percent of Kone's business and was growing as a portion of total group business in Europe and the U.S.
Steps to restore profitability to Kone's loss-making Italian operations would be a priority for this year, he said.
"We will begin to break even in Italy some time later this year, but that does not mean that the cumulative result for the full year (by the Italian operations) will be positive," he said.
Kone will also launch a new European elevator model based on its space-saving EcoDisc technology this year, Soila said.
Kone has begun testing the technology -- already used in a concept launched in Europe last year -- in skyscraper lifts, he said, adding: "It looks very promising."
